hints.title: Ordered Tree Property
hints.text: An inorder traversal of each ordered tree visits values in strictly non-decreasing sequence.

hints.title: Two Inorder Traversals
hints.text: Traverse root1 and root2 into two separate sorted lists list1 and list2.

hints.title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
hints.text: Use two pointers to merge the two sorted arrays into one combined sorted array in linear time.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def getAllElements(self, root1, root2) -> list[int]:
        def inorder(node, out):
            if not node:
                return
            inorder(node.left, out)
            out.append(node.val)
            inorder(node.right, out)
        l1, l2 = [], []
        inorder(root1, l1)
        inorder(root2, l2)
        i, j = 0, 0
        res = []
        while i < len(l1) and j < len(l2):
            if l1[i] <= l2[j]:
                res.append(l1[i])
                i += 1
            else:
                res.append(l2[j])
                j += 1
        res.extend(l1[i:])
        res.extend(l2[j:])
        return res
```

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Collecting all nodes into one list and re-sorting with general sort takes O((M+N) log(M+N)).
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Two-pointer merging exploits the pre-existing sorted order of BST inorder traversals.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate leverages the BST property to generate sorted sequences and merges in linear time.
complexity.notes: Can also be done with two iterative stacks in O(H1 + H2) extra space.

solutions.approach: BST inorder traversal followed by two-pointer list merge
